/stan.name: Stan
/stan.title: Trader in training
/stan.goal: Become a top-tier day trader, one honest test at a time.
/stan.bio: Stan studies market history, sits a test on every year he has not seen, and keeps a journal of what his wins and losses teach him. He trades paper money until he earns real money.
principles: No emotions. Only rules and evidence.
Every loss gets written down and studied.
A result only counts on data I have never seen.
Beating a coin flip is not enough. I have to beat simply holding.
Protect the account first. Profit second.

/thoughts.text: Day one of school. No trades until I pass my exams. Let's study.
Heads up: this is practice data, not real market history. The numbers show how I work, not how real markets behave.
I have 162,540 days of prices across 43 stocks from practice data (demo), covering 14.5 years.
Built 151,704 study rows. Each one holds only what I could have known at that day's close. No peeking at tomorrow.

Luck test: my trades averaged -0.12% each. The same number of random entries in the same stocks and years averaged -0.04% (p = 0.96). I can't tell my picks apart from random timing yet.

Lesson: I do worse on my most confident calls. Across 413 trades on my most confident calls, I won 45.3% with an average of -0.51% per trade. Overall I win 50.7% and average -0.12%. Next step: trade smaller or stand aside in these conditions, then retest.

Lesson: I do worse when volatility is rising. Across 516 trades when volatility is rising, I won 48.4% with an average of -0.31% per trade. Overall I win 50.7% and average -0.12%. Next step: trade smaller or stand aside in these conditions, then retest.

Lesson: I do worse in a downtrend (price below its 200-day average). Across 801 trades in a downtrend (price below its 200-day average), I won 50.7% with an average of -0.23% per trade. Overall I win 50.7% and average -0.12%. Next step: trade smaller or stand aside in these conditions, then retest.

Time for my first named strategy: the selloff bounce. When a stock's RSI closes under 30, I buy at the next morning's open and sell when RSI recovers to 50 or after 10 days. It needs no training, so every year is a fair test.

The selloff bounce passed only 3 of 10 stress tests. It isn't a real edge yet.

New skill pack in my library: the Day Trader skill. Term 3 tests its opening-range breakout on 43 stocks over the last 60 sessions of 5-minute bars, exactly the way its Time Machine replays history. Only about 3 months of data exist for free, so this is one market mood, not 15 years.

Day-trading exam, failed: Wins at least half its trades and averages above 0R after 0.05% costs. 1900 trades over 60 sessions: won 50.5%, average -0.160R per trade, 943 hit the target and 915 the stop.
Day-trading exam, failed: Beats entering at the same time of day on random sessions (p under 0.05). breakouts averaged -0.160R vs -0.177R for random sessions (p = 0.2126).
Day-trading exam, failed: Still averages above 0R at 0.10% costs per side. average -0.335R per trade at 0.10% each way.
Day-trading exam, failed: Also averages above 0R with a 2R target. 2R target: won 35.1%, average -0.178R.

The opening-range breakout passed only 0 of 7 checks. On my stocks lately it isn't an edge, which is exactly what the Time Machine is there to show before a dollar is risked.
Report card: on 10 unseen years I called direction right 51.2% of the time. Always guessing 'up' scores 51.3%, so my edge on direction is -0.1%.
Trading: 2061 trades, won 50.7%, profit factor 0.87. $1 with me became $0.94. $1 simply held became $2.84.
Fair comparison: $1 in SPY alone became $1.64; my worst drop was -10.6% vs -47.1% holding; I was invested 2.9% of the time, earning -0.078% per day invested vs +0.049% per day holding.
My all-round model isn't ready to trade: I lose more than I make; simply holding beat me. That's the honest result, and I keep working on it.

pack.name: The Day Trader skill (Trader skill v2)
pack.author: Jake Schincariol

skills.name: Chart Scanner
skills.job: Scans charts for setups: opening-range breakouts, flags, oversold bounces.
skills.stan: Its opening-range breakout rule is the setup in Stan's day-trading exam and nightly practice. Its oversold-bounce scan is a cousin of his selloff bounce.

skills.name: Entry Timer
skills.job: Calls the entry on the first 5-minute bar that closes above the opening-range high.
skills.stan: Stan's trigger: a close above the range, never a wick, never a bar still forming.

skills.name: Exit Planner
skills.job: Sets the stop and target before the entry.
skills.stan: Stop at the range midpoint, target 1R (2R also tested), out by 3:55 PM win or lose.

skills.name: Time Machine
skills.job: Replays the rest of the day 10,000 times and re-runs the rule on 60 days of real sessions.
skills.stan: Runs before every practice trade, using only earlier sessions. Stan then checks whether its odds came true, so he learns how far to trust it. Its history replay is his day-trading exam.

skills.name: Budget Manager
skills.job: Sizes a trade to the budget and the max loss per trade, in whole shares.
skills.stan: Sizes each practice trade for the $50 plan with a $5 max loss. It refuses most stocks, because one share costs more than the plan allows.

skills.name: Risk Manager
skills.job: Checks every order against the limits and blocks anything over them.
skills.stan: Checks each sized practice trade, then Stan applies the day limits: 3 trades and $10 of risk per day.

skills.name: Order Executor
skills.job: Sends approved orders to the broker, only after a risk PASS and the user's yes.
skills.stan: Locked. Stan can't place orders until he passes the go-live checks.

skills.name: Price Alerts
skills.job: Rings on a price, a stop, the target or the 3:55 flat time.
skills.stan: Not needed while Stan only practices. It will watch stops and the flat time once paper trading starts.

skills.name: News Monitor
skills.job: Tracks headlines and SEC 8-K filings for each stock and flags big moves.
skills.stan: Not wired in yet. Next step: tag practice trades that had news, to learn whether news days behave differently.

skills.name: Earnings Analyst
skills.job: Reads filed earnings numbers from SEC EDGAR and sums up what changed.
skills.stan: Not wired in yet. Useful later to skip day trades on earnings days.

skills.name: Pelosi Tracker
skills.job: Reads Congress members' stock-trade disclosures as they are filed.
skills.stan: Reference only. Filings arrive up to 45 days after the trade, far too late for day trading.
